newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - March 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - March 31.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Negotiations between Pakistan and India went into the third day despite the political crisis threatening to topple the Indian government.
- The government is considering a proposal to restrict trade union activities in commercial banks as part of its large scale banking reforms, sources said.

- Several Arab militants belonging to Egypt-based Takfiri group have gone into hiding and taken refuge at the secret abodes of some Afghan guerrilla commanders following Thursday's killing of its six members by the police at Jalozai camp.
- Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto has said the economic package announced by the government on Friday was a sell out to business interests.
- Benazir Bhutto has accused President Farooq Leghari of denying hospitalisation to her interned husband, Senator-elect Asif Ali Zardari.
- Teachers of all public sector universities in Sindh province will launch a protest movement from April 10 if the ban on the appointment of teachers is not lifted.

- Prime Minister Naweaz Sharif has played the biggest political gamble of his life by offering an economic package that seeks to oblige business community by giving it unprecedented concessions and exemptions and to revive the 4,000 sick industrial units.

- The first meeting of the newly-constituted Federal Export Development Board will be held on April 9 to tackle the whole gamut of issues which are affecting the growth of exports. Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif will preside at the meeting.

- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif in his address to the nation over the electronic media on Monday evening is likely to appeal to the public to promote a tax culture to tide over economic problems on a permanent basis.

- The net investment in lease finance of the 30 issues listed at the Karachi Stock Exchange has increased to 20.61 billion rupees as on June 30, 1996 from 8.87 billion in 1993 on an average annual growth rate of 33 percent.

- Cut in corporate tax will boost the profits of the listed companies at the stock market while exemptions in raw material imports appear to target foreign direct investment, leading brokerage houses said.
